title: Policy on Key Management Personnel Dealing in Securities

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Those persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any Director (whether executive or otherwise), per the AASB 124 definition adopted by the ASX Listing Rules. Subject to the closed period, clearance and short-term dealing rules.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A subset of Key Management Personnel; distinguished only by faster/direct post-trade notification to the Company Secretary and personal ASX Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z and Corporations Act s205G notification obligations.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman, a Director; distinguished only for pre-clearance approval, which is given by two independent Non-Executive Directors and the Company Secretary rather than the Chairman/Company Secretary route used by other Key Management Personnel.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Not separately defined; Key Management Personnel 'dealing' is stated to include dealing by their associates, and each member must ensure an associate does not deal in circumstances attributable to them.

windows.start_anchor: 1 month prior to the release of annual or half-yearly results
windows.end_anchor: release of the relevant annual or half-yearly results (Key Management Personnel should also wait at least 24 hours after release before dealing)

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named. 'Deal in securities' is defined broadly to include entering into transactions 'in relation to' shares, options or other securities, which would sweep in an OTC put/call referencing Company shares and subject it to the same prior written clearance and closed-period rules.
rules.evidence: "deal in securities" means apply for, buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging, and unvested equity incentive securities generally, are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement would be a transaction 'in relation to' shares and so a dealing requiring the same clearance.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named; they would be a transaction 'in relation to' shares and so a dealing requiring clearance, and could also be caught by the undefined short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements generally are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Absolute ban on short-term trading, but the policy does not define what period counts as short-term (unlike the more common fixed 3-month rule).
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

clearance.approver: Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: they have contacted the Chairman or, in his absence, the Company Secretary and notified them of their intention to do so and the Chairman or Company Secretary gives them written clearance to do so. ... Other Key Management Personnel are required to notify the Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary of any dealings in securities within 5 business days.

clearance.approver: Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary (same pre-clearance route as other Key Management Personnel)
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify the Company Secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.

clearance.approver: Two independent Non-Executive Directors and the Company Secretary, in consultation
clearance.evidence: where the Chairman wishes to deal in securities, he has contacted two independent Non-Executive Directors and the Company Secretary and the Company Secretary, in consultation with the two Directors, gives the Chairman written clearance to do so.

short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: suffering severe financial hardship such that dealing in securities is the only reasonable course of action available (for example, selling the securities is the only way to satisfy a pressing financial commitment)

exceptions.approver: Chairman, or in his absence, the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: other exceptional circumstances exist such that dealing in securities is the only reasonable course of action available. Such circumstances may include, for example, circumstances that compel the Key Management Personnel to deal in securities, such as a court order, a bona fide enforceable undertaking to a court or other legal or regulatory requirement.

exemption_authority: Key Management Personnel should consider this policy binding 'in the absence of specific exemption by the Board' (2.2); no procedure, criteria or confidentiality treatment is specified for such a Board exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "deal in securities" means apply for, buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This 2010-era policy never mentions derivatives, hedging, margin lending, secured financing or collateral by name, so a funded collar and its loan leg would be regulated, if at all, only through this single broad 'transaction in relation to' phrase, leaving real interpretive uncertainty over the financing leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should wait at least 24 hours after the relevant release before dealing in securities so that the market has had time to absorb the information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Non-binding ('should') but relevant to timing the collar's entry immediately after results are released, on top of the formal closed period ending at release.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Suggests the Board could grant a bespoke exemption to facilitate a collar structure, though no process is specified.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel "dealing" includes associates of Key Management Personnel dealing in securities, and it is incumbent on each member of Key Management Personnel to ensure that an associate does not deal in circumstances where the dealing could be attributed to the member concerned.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written through a spouse, family trust or related entity would still be attributed to the Key Management Personnel member and subject to the same clearance and closed-period rules.

summary: This 2010-era Mount Gibson policy never mentions derivatives, hedging, margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs, so an OTC put/call and its secured loan are caught, if at all, only through the broad definition of 'deal in securities' as including 'transactions in relation to' shares. On that basis a funded collar could be entered by Key Management Personnel (including Directors) with prior written clearance from the Chairman or Company Secretary, or by the Chairman with clearance from two independent Non-Executive Directors and the Company Secretary, executed within 7 days of clearance and outside the 1-month closed periods before annual/half-yearly results, absent a hardship or court-order exemption. The loan/pledge leg has no dedicated regime at all - nothing on collateralising the shares, forced sales, margin calls or financing disclosure - so its permissibility depends entirely on whether granting security is treated as a 'transaction in relation to' the shares, which is untested. Directors also carry personal ASX Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z and Corporations Act s205G notification duties, and no dealing may be short-term (an undefined duration). Overall a funded collar is plausible under the general clearance and closed-period regime but carries meaningful interpretive risk on the secured-financing leg because the policy is simply silent on it.
